Maxx Crosby showed out in Week 10, racking up seven solos, one assist, one sack, and four tackles for loss. Crosby started the season slow in the sack department, but has now registered one in each of his last three games. Start Maxx with confidence for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Denver Broncos.

George Karlaftis was back at it in Week 10, tallying two solos, two assists, 1.5 sacks, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Furious George is up to 5.5 sacks on the season, with all of them coming in his last five games (4.5 in the last three). Fire Karlaftis up as a top-20 option as long as he stays cooking. Start the Chiefs edge rusher everywhere.

Jaelan Phillips stepped up in Week 10, racking up four solos, one assist, one sack, three tackles for loss, and one fumble recovery. Phillips is up to 3.5 sacks, with at least a half sack in four of his five games played. Jaelan is a DL2 option when he is actually on the field, but staying healthy continues to be an issue for the talented edge rusher. Tap Phillips as a top-25 option for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Chop Robinson was excellent in Week 10, reeling off three solos, two assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Start him everywhere for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Buffalo Bills.

Adetomiwa Adebawore stepped up in Week 10, notching one solo, two assists, one fumble recovery, and one touchdown. Adebawore has worked his way into the DT1 conversation and sits at a cool four sacks on the season. The Colts defensive lineman can also be counted as a DL3/4 option during the heavy bye. Start him where needed for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football.

DJ Wonnum stepped up in Week 10, racking up three solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Wonnum is healthy and no longer has to deal with the threat of ceding snaps to Derrick Moore due to Aidan Hutchinson being lost for the year. Ashton Gillotte stepped up in Week 10, tallying two solos, three assists, one sack, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended. Derrick Moore was at it again in Week 10, tallying two solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Moore has caught fire for the Lions, recording two sacks in back-to-back games. Start him with confidence where needed for a plus Week 11 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Levi Drake Rodriguez stepped up in Week 10, posting two solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. It was the third sack of the season for Levi, but his first since all the way back in Week 1. Rodriguez plays a healthy amount of snaps, which helps keep him on the DT3/4, but his limited sack production keeps him out of the DL mix. Look elsewhere for Week 11.

Shelby Harris stepped up in Week 10, racking up three solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Harris has just the one sack on the season and is not yet on the fantasy radar in any format. Look elsewhere for Week 11.

Dalvin Tomlinson had himself a game against the Baltimore Ravens, racking up three solos, two assists, two sacks, and two tackles for loss. Tomlinson had not done much prior to this, but does play enough snaps to be considered a DT who can get some DL depth love in 32-team leagues.
